conviction_note: The reported quarter should land at or slightly above a bar the Street has already cut below management's own +$40-50M sequential EBITDA guide: peers report higher realized prices and lower scrap over June-August, so print_vs_bar is about +2%. The stock trades on the forward read, though, and the Q1 FY27 inputs lean against it. Korean rebar imports kept rising through July when management said they would fall, mills gave concessions on large volumes in early September, and scrap is expected to rise about 6.6% in October with no rebar price increase found. Last October's print fell 7.26% on a beat. So p_up is 45 on an abs move of 5.5 (option-implied 5.04, raised because a new-period outlook is likely), giving -0.55, close to the findings' sum of -0.6. The two numbers disagree in sign (beat, but stock down) because the guide outweighs the quarter on this name.
bar: Q4 FY26 adjusted EPS consensus $1.96 from 9 analysts (AAII/S&P/IBES, 2026-10-14, https://www.aaii.com/investingideas/article/507487-what-you-need-to-know-about-commercial-metals-companys-q4-earnings), with $1.97 from Earnings Whispers (https://beta.earningswhispers.com/go/w/CMC) and $1.91 from Zacks; revenue about $2.54-2.55B. The company guide is a $40-50M sequential overall EBITDA improvement on Q3 core EBITDA of $353.6M and adjusted EPS of $1.73, net of the absent $20.4M CO2 credit and West Virginia start-up costs (https://earningswhispers.com/transcript/CMC/Q32026). By my arithmetic the guide implies about $2.00-2.05, so consensus already sits slightly below it.
positioning_check: Short interest was about 4.7M shares (about 4% of float) with about 3.6 days to cover at the 2026-07-15 FINRA settlement. That figure is from a curvedtrading.com search snippet; the page was 403 and the later September settlements were not retrievable (https://curvedtrading.com/stocks/cmc/short-interest/). It is down from 6.5M shares and 7.7 days at 2026-04-30. Not crowded, so no squeeze adjustment. The baseline skew is +9.42 vol points (downside paid) on a thin chain with a 62% ATM spread; put/call OI is 0.39. Sell-side cut targets into the print: Wells Fargo $80 to $68 (2026-10-06) and JPMorgan $83 to $80 (2026-10-09) (https://www.marketbeat.com/stocks/NYSE/CMC/price-target/). The stock is down 12.6% since the June print while SPY rose 6.0% (AAII).

findings.finding: Peers that spoke after CMC confirm a widening steel metal margin over CMC's fiscal Q4 (June-August). Steel Dynamics guided on 2026-09-17 to higher realized steel selling values with lower scrap costs. Nucor guided to higher steel-mills selling prices. SMU puts August shredded at $417.50/gt, down $5 from July, against March Ohio Valley shredded of $445-450 in CMC's Q3. US rebar rose 0.96% in July and was flat in August. That supports CMC delivering the top of its +$40-50M sequential EBITDA guide, against a consensus (~$1.96) below the guide-implied ~$2.00-2.05.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q3 FY26 (2026-06-25), a small EPS beat with a stronger-Q4 outlook: +3.94%. Q4 FY25 (2025-10-16), an EPS beat ($1.37 vs $1.34, per TheFly via TipRanks): -7.26%, so a fiscal-Q4 beat has been sold before. Q2 FY26 miss: -4.69%.
findings.why_not_priced: Consensus at $1.96 sits below what management's own +$40-50M guide implies, and AAII records one estimate cut and no raises in the last month. Partly priced: the peer read is a month old and lands inside what CMC guided, so it is sized small. If priced, consensus would sit at or above $2.03.
findings.independence: Separate sources point the same way. Nucor Q3 guidance of 2026-09-17 (steel mills: higher average selling prices): https://s202.q4cdn.com/531038915/files/doc_news/Nucor-Announces-Guidance-for-the-Third-Quarter-of-2026-Earnings-2026.pdf. SMU August scrap, via search snippet: https://www.steelmarketupdate.com/2026/08/11/smu-scrap-prices-stagnant-in-august/. ChemAnalyst rebar, 2026-08-20: https://www.chemanalyst.com/NewsAndDeals/NewsDetails/us-steel-rebar-prices-stay-range-bound-as-buyers-adopt-44010. Against: management guided West Virginia start-up costs to roughly double to about $8-10M a quarter, which is already inside the $40-50M (https://earningswhispers.com/transcript/CMC/Q32026). This is a proxy; neither peer breaks out rebar.

findings.finding: US rebar imports from South Korea kept rising through CMC's fiscal Q4 rather than falling as management expected in June: 95,054 mt in June and 104,147 mt in July, against 5,071 mt in July 2025. Total July imports were 112,306 mt, up 84.6% YoY, at an implied ~$525/mt unit value. June plus July alone (199k mt) nearly match all of fiscal Q3 (about 213k mt). GMK (2026-09-17) reports import availability held US rebar back in early September, with mills conceding on large volumes. That points to a cautious Q1 FY27 pricing and margin outlook.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The fiscal-Q4 print with its Q1 seasonal outlook fell 7.26% on 2025-10-16 despite an EPS beat. Q1 FY26 (2026-01-08) fell 3.56%. Q2 FY26 (2026-03-26) fell 4.69% on a miss with margin pressure.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: the stock is down 12.6% since June, Wells Fargo cut its target to $68 on 2026-10-06, and the skew pays for downside. What is not in the wire copy is that the import series now contradicts management's June statement that Korean imports would fall in the second half. If fully priced, Q1 consensus would already embed a lower metal margin, and preview notes would cite the July Census number. None of the previews found does.
findings.independence: Management's own June statement on Korean imports is the baseline being contradicted: https://earningswhispers.com/transcript/CMC/Q32026. A separate trade-press source on early-September concessions (search snippet; the page was 403): https://gmk.center/en/news/key-global-markets-are-set-for-a-rise-in-rebar-prices/. This finding agrees with the skew, so it is partly priced.

findings.finding: Fastmarkets' October 2026 US scrap outlook (published 2026-09-30) expects scrap up about 6.6% month on month, on higher demand, tighter inventory and export pull. Rebar has no matching price increase in the record: the only October long-product increase found is $50/st on beams (Nucor-Yamato, Gerdau). So the cost side squeezes the Q1 FY27 metal margin that management will guide to.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q3 FY26: a scrap cost rise of +$28/t outran the +$15/t price rise and metal margin fell $13/t sequentially. The stock still rose 3.94% on the stronger-Q4 outlook. Q2 FY26 margin pressure: -4.69%.
findings.why_not_priced: This is a survey outlook for one month, behind a trade-press paywall, and is not in any CMC preview found. If priced, previews would flag Q1 margin compression and the stock would not have bounced 2.1% in the last five sessions. Sized small because it is a proxy, and CMC may raise rebar prices to pass the cost through.
findings.independence: The absence of an October rebar increase rests on search results only. The beam increase is GMK, 2026-10-02 (snippet; 403): https://gmk.center/en/news/nucor-yamato-and-gerdau-have-raised-their-prices-for-beams-in-the-us/. This is not the same fact as the import finding (cost side against price side), but both feed one Q1 margin outlook, so together they should not be read as two independent negatives.

findings.finding: Expectations were reset lower into the print. Wells Fargo cut its target from $80 to $68 (2026-10-06) and JPMorgan from $83 to $80 (2026-10-09). AAII shows one Q4 estimate cut and no raises in the last month. The stock is 22% off its 52-week high and down 12.6% since the June print while SPY rose 6%.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The June 2026 print came after an estimate cut-down (consensus fell from $2.00 to $1.60 per Barchart) and the stock rose 3.94% on a modest beat.
findings.why_not_priced: This is positioning, not information. It lowers the bar the reaction is measured against, and it argues a meet-the-guide quarter is less likely to be sold hard. Mostly priced by definition; small.

findings.finding: CMC holds about $717M of buyback authorization after the incremental $600M approved at the 2026-08-05 Investor Day, roughly 10% of its market cap at $64.58. Fiscal Q3 repurchases were only $18.9M, so the Q4 repurchase figure and the FY27 capital-return language disclosed with the print may step up.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No resolved history on this line. The authorization itself (2026-08-05) was followed by target raises (BMO, Barclays) and the stock opening near $75.78.
findings.why_not_priced: The authorization is public; the pace is not. An inference only, so it is sized small. If priced, nothing would look different.
findings.independence: Q3 repurchase pace from the Q3 release: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000022444/000002244426000038/cmc-5312026xearningsreleas.htm. Same company; inference.

findings.finding: European steel conditions improved over the summer. Polish peer Cognor reported H1 2026 net profit of PLN 5.7M against a loss of PLN 26.5M, on better spreads and volumes, after raising rebar prices about 20% since January. CBAM and EU trade measures took effect on 2026-07-01, which CMC said would support Europe.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No separable history; Europe is about 5-10% of core EBITDA.
findings.source_date: 2026 H1 results (date from snippet; page not opened)
findings.why_not_priced: It sits inside management's guide of 'modestly higher Europe ex-CO2', and the segment is small net of North America. Close to zero.

searched_and_found_nothing: EDGAR since the Q3 8-K: the only 8-Ks are the 2026-08-05 Investor Day and the 2026-10-13 dividend (unchanged at $0.20). No pre-announcement, no item 2.05/2.06, no outage disclosure.
The Form 4 cluster on 2026-10-13/14 is routine: settlement of October 2023 performance shares, tax withholding at $63.89, and new RSU grants dated 2026-10-12. No open-market buys or sales.
No 2026 CMC mill outage, fire or incident found at Seguin, Mesa, Sayreville, Durant or West Virginia.
No October 2026 rebar price increase or cut from CMC, Nucor or Gerdau found; only beams +$50.
No August 2026 US rebar import figure published yet.
No new AD/CVD petition against Korean rebar found (the Korea AD order was revoked in an earlier sunset review).
No September short-interest settlement retrievable (Nasdaq 503, curvedtrading 403).
No Q4 key-metric consensus (NASG shipments, metal margin) retrievable (Zacks bot wall).
Barchart's 'downward revisions' piece turned out to be the June Q3 preview, not a Q4 one.

baseline_tension: The negatives agree with the +9.4 downside skew and with a stock already down 12.6% since June, so they are partly priced and sized small. The positives (peer margin read, expectations reset) cut against the skew but land inside the company's guide. Net, a slight lean toward the skew.
lessons_applied: Lessons 1 and 6 (a verified fact is not a predicted reaction; findings inside the guided range): the peer metal-margin finding lands inside management's +$40-50M guide, and this name fell 7.26% on last October's beat, so +0.6 became +0.3.

Lesson 7 (a sign that agrees with the skew is partly priced): the Korea-imports finding agrees with the +9.4 skew and the 12.6% decline, so -1.2 became -1.0. It was kept rather than shrunk further because it contradicts management's own stated expectation.
Lesson 5 (a proxy is filed small): the October scrap outlook is a one-month survey proxy, so -0.6 became -0.5.
Lesson 9 (size a segment finding net of the rest): Europe is about 5-10% of EBITDA and inside the guide, so +0.2 became +0.1.
Lesson 7 (look up short interest before a negative): about 4% of float and 3.6 days to cover, not crowded, so no squeeze haircut. p_up stays 45 and abs_move 5.5.
